places.name: Classic Diner
places.notes: Neon signs buzz outside. Patrons read physical newspapers. Cash register has a bulky CRT monitor.

places.name: Indie Coffee Shop
places.notes: Students use thick laptops connected to early Wi-Fi. Bulletin board has tear-off flyers for local indie bands.

places.name: Slice Pizzeria
places.notes: Open late for bar-hoppers. A small CRT TV mounted in the corner plays sports.

places.name: Corner Deli
places.notes: A landline phone sits behind the counter for delivery orders. Heavy use of physical cash.

places.name: Dive Bar
places.notes: Jukebox is loaded with CDs. Cigarette machine still in the corner, though smoking bans are starting to hit.

places.name: Neighborhood Bakery
places.notes: No laptops, just locals buying daily bread. Staff tracks custom cake orders in a spiral notebook.

places.name: Upscale Bistro
places.notes: Patrons check their BlackBerries during dinner. Payments made with magnetic stripe credit cards.

places.name: Fast Food Burger Joint
places.notes: Heavy plastic aesthetic. Early thick LCD menus above the POS systems.

places.name: Chinese Takeout
places.notes: Stack of paper menus on the counter. A wired telephone constantly rings for delivery orders.

places.name: Chain Pharmacy
places.notes: Features a digital photo printing kiosk where people plug in SD cards or USB drives.

places.name: Bodega
places.notes: Sells international prepaid calling cards and physical newspapers. Dusty CRT TV behind the counter.

places.name: Consumer Electronics Store
places.notes: Dominant items are standalone GPS units for cars, 4GB MP3 players, and early heavy 720p flat screens.

places.name: Mobile Phone Kiosk
places.notes: Walls covered in plastic cases for Motorola Razrs and BlackBerries. Promotes 'Unlimited T9 Texting'.

places.name: Newsstand
places.notes: Print media is still highly relevant. Gossip magazines mock early 2000s celebrities.

places.name: Coin Laundromat
places.notes: People read physical books or listen to iPods while waiting. Requires quarters, no card readers on machines.

places.name: Pawn Shop
places.notes: Iron bars on windows. Heavy inventory of used car stereos, DVDs, and older game consoles.

places.name: DVD & Video Rental
places.notes: Dying breed but still surviving in 2008. Lots of 'Be Kind, Rewind' stickers on older VHS stock being sold off.

places.name: Record & CD Store
places.notes: CDs are still the main seller, but vinyl is making an indie comeback. Listening stations let you preview tracks.

places.name: Used Bookstore
places.notes: Smells like old paper. No e-readers around, just physical books. Cash register is an old mechanical one.

places.name: Hardware Store
places.notes: Dusty and cluttered. Receipts are printed on dot-matrix printers.

places.name: Dance Nightclub
places.notes: Digital cameras everywhere using harsh flashes. DJ is spinning CDs or vinyl, no laptop.

places.name: Karaoke Lounge
places.notes: Thick songbook binders filled with laminated pages. Bulky microphones with physical cords.

places.name: Retro Arcade
places.notes: Still surviving in 2008 through rhythm games and fighting game tournaments. Very loud CRT buzz.

places.name: Indie Cinema
places.notes: Projects physical 35mm film. Patrons carry flip phones and wait in line outside.

places.name: Pool & Billiards Hall
places.notes: Chalk dust in the air. People pay for table time by the hour using cash.

places.name: Comedy Club
places.notes: Brick wall behind the stage. No smartphones to record sets, though some might sneak a flip phone picture.

places.name: Cybercafe
places.notes: Loud clicking of mechanical keyboards and gamers playing LAN matches on beige/black PC towers.

places.name: Print & Copy Center
places.notes: People still rely heavily on fax machines for official documents. USB drives are common for printing.

places.name: Local Bank Branch
places.notes: Tellers use older AS400-style green screen terminal interfaces or early Windows XP banking software.

places.name: Classic Barbershop
places.notes: CRT TV in the corner is always tuned to ESPN or local news. Thick sports magazines on the table.

places.name: Budget Motel
places.notes: Free Wi-Fi is heavily advertised as a new premium feature, but connections drop constantly.

places.name: Fitness Gym
places.notes: People listen to music on iPod Nanos strapped to their arms with velcro bands.

places.name: Dental Clinic
places.notes: Patient records are highly reliant on massive physical manila folders kept behind the reception desk.

places.name: Police Precinct
places.notes: Desks are cluttered with paperwork, bulky radios, and thick CRT monitors. Ashtrays still visible but unused.

places.name: Post Office
places.notes: Stamp price in 2008 is 42 cents. A heavy matrix printer grinds away at receipts.

places.name: Small Law Firm
places.notes: Conference room table features a bulky Polycom star-shaped conference phone. Blackberrys buzz silently on desks.

places.name: Accounting Firm
places.notes: Physical adding machines with paper tape are still widely used alongside Excel 2003/2007.

places.name: Insurance Agency
places.notes: Desks have large Rolodexes and thick phone books. Agents use heavy beige corded phones.

places.name: Call Center
places.notes: Loud hum of voices and AC. Agents are using wired headsets connected to bulky IP phones.

places.name: Boutique Ad Agency
places.notes: Heavy use of early aluminum iMacs. Employees playing ping pong or listening to iPods at their desks.

places.name: Indie Software Dev
places.notes: Developers drinking energy drinks, writing code on Windows XP or early OS X. Xbox 360 in the lounge for Halo 3 breaks.

places.name: Corporate Satellite Office
places.notes: Grey, soul-crushing beige aesthetic. Floppy disks are dead, but CD-RWs and USB thumb drives are everywhere.

places.name: Auto Mechanic Garage
places.notes: Grease everywhere. The shop radio blasts classic rock. Diagnostics run on specialized heavy rugged laptops.

places.name: Commercial Print Shop
places.notes: Smells heavily of ink and ozone. Graphic files are submitted via CD-ROMs or early slow FTP servers.

places.name: Warehouse Storage
places.notes: Echoey and dusty. Workers use rugged barcode scanners with monochrome green screens.

places.name: Scrap Yard Office
places.notes: Office is a prefabricated trailer. Walls are covered in faded pin-up calendars and parts catalogs.

places.name: Studio Apartment
places.notes: Cramped living space. A Nintendo Wii or PS2 sits under the thick TV. Broadband router blinks in the corner.

places.name: 1-Bedroom Apartment
places.notes: Standard young professional home. Stacks of DVD cases next to the TV. Desktop PC in the bedroom corner.

places.name: 2-Bedroom Family Apartment
places.notes: Family home. Landline phone on the kitchen wall. Messy desk with a shared family Dell PC running Windows Vista.

places.name: SRO / Tenement Room
places.notes: Single Room Occupancy. Bathrooms are shared in the hallway (not in the room). Rabbit ear antenna on the TV.

places.name: Brownstone Floor
places.notes: Wealthy urban living. Flat screen TVs (plasma or early LCD) are a status symbol here. iPod docking station on the shelf.

places.name: Luxury Penthouse
places.notes: High-end 2008 luxury. Home theater systems with Blu-Ray players. Clean, minimalist furniture.
